page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 40 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a baseline clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 4.8 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on external storage solutions and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. In CPU-intensive tasks, it achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and compression capabilities are solid, with a PassMark encryption score of 17622.01 and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 25.12 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is well-suited for database operations, software compilation, and web serving. It achieves 34.78 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 25.35 GB/sec. However, the lack of bundled local storage and GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for heavy local storage-dependent databases or large-scale deep learning training, though it can handle smaller LLM inference tasks, processing 56.94 tokens per second for a 7B model prompt.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server featuring 40 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. It is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM (4.8 GB per core), 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage or GPU accelerators. In performance testing, the instance delivers balanced results, including a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 38378.07. It shows strong throughput in database and web serving workloads, achieving 34.78 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 25.35 GB/sec in static web serving. The dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed make this instance highly efficient for compute-heavy general-purpose workloads, software compilation, and medium-scale database hosting, though the absence of local NVMe storage requires external storage attachments.
